_comment: Machine-readable form of docs/ASSET_SPEC.md. The contract is source-agnostic: it describes what
an asset must satisfy to work in this engine, not where the asset came from. Dawn of War II is
reference implementation #1 (see docs/METHOD_PORTABILITY.md); our own art is adapter #2.
Labels used throughout: measured = read from shipped data, engine = required by the shipped
engine as encoded in the community exporter's validation, choice = a decision of this project.
`budgets` is cross-checked against tools/glb_contract.py LIMITS by tools/spec/validate_assets.py
so the prose, this file and the gate cannot drift apart.

collision.simple: walkable faces only, world normal within N degrees of up
collision.complex: projectile and unit nav, garrisonable structures

terrain.weight_packing: layer i weight = mask[i // 4] channel i % 4 (RGBA)
terrain.activity_grid: layer i active = usage[i // 4] channel i % 4 (RGBA)
terrain.blend: weighted accumulation normalised by total weight, epsilon 1e-5

heightmap.format: u32 width, u32 height, zlib float grid

terrain.label: engine

map.container: chunk tree, 4-byte tags with sizes and offsets
map.placement: blueprint index into a path table + 4x3 transform
map.label: measured

gaps: hkanim additive layering and motiontree state machines
collision simple/complex meshes (cover volumes only today)
simbox physics hulls (static props ship with no body)
terrain layer blending in the forge (single texture today)
RSH atlas composition (reads _dif.dds directly, ignores channel packing)
specular/gloss maps not yet authored for our own art

_comment: A limit is only a requirement for us if it is a limit of OUR target engine or of the vertex
format. A limit of the source engine (DoW2, D3D9) must be recorded, not imposed: building our
own art to it would discard headroom for no reason, and failing imported art against it would
report a defect that is not one.

universal.because: vertex attribute format (4 indices + 4 weights) and the target engine's own hard limit
sources: three.js: max 4 bones influencing a vertex (mrdoob/three.js issue 26137, discourse 47457)
DoW2 exporter truncates to the strongest 4 (dow2_tools/model/exporter_meshes.py:325)

target_engine.name: WebGL2 / three.js
target_engine.because: WebGL2 guarantees GL_MAX_UNIFORM_BLOCK_SIZE of 16 KB; the bone matrix block is 64 bytes per bone, so 256 is the guaranteed minimum (mrdoob/three.js issue 34196)

source_engine_only.name: DoW2 / D3D9
source_engine_only.because: D3D9 shader constant and sampler budgets; recorded, not imposed on our art
source_engine_only.measured_breaches_in_shipped_content: 17 converted units exceed 54 joints (55-110); they render correctly in our engine, which allows 256

provenance._comment: UVs are required exactly when there is a texture to sample. An imported asset that ships no texture at all is a flat-colour asset: its lack of UVs is a measured property of the source, reported and counted, not a failure.
